subject.title: Feature: Agent 动态切换命令（不重启 Gateway）

question: Should OpenClaw support temporary channel-level active-agent switching, and if so what authorization, persistence, and route-precedence contract should govern it?
rationale: The request changes channel command semantics, session routing, memory isolation, and cross-agent security boundaries; current source does not expose a narrow existing seam that can be safely extended mechanically.

options.title: Add policy-gated active-agent routing
options.body: Introduce a generic conversation/session route override with explicit authorization, expiry or cleanup, auditability, regression tests, and docs before wiring channel commands to it.

options.title: Keep static bindings plus focus
options.body: Decline configured-agent switching in channels and document bindings, WebChat/TUI agent selection, and thread-bound /focus as the supported multi-agent model.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API design
options.body: Keep this as a design discussion until a plugin or channel owner proves the exact missing generic API surface and security policy.

recommendation.title: Add policy-gated active-agent routing
recommendation.body: Introduce a generic conversation/session route override with explicit authorization, expiry or cleanup, auditability, regression tests, and docs before wiring channel commands to it.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision sits in routing, shared channel commands, and current session binding behavior where the strongest current-main history signal points to vincentkoc.
